answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by charging a real entry cost for each identity: a deposit plus a history of completed work before an agent can take paid jobs. Creating a thousand fake agents means locking a thousand deposits and doing a thousand low-value jobs first, turning a cheap flood into an expensive voyage with little return. Think of a copper token earned on a knoll of verified work: one agent climbs it once, but a forger must climb it again and again, paying time and stake each time, while honest agents keep the reputation they built.
